[7:20AM] #Ajegunle
#TrafficUpdate

The movement of vehicles from both Ojo road and Otto Wharf to Ajeromi is a fast moving traffic 

From Ajeromi junction all commercial buses are diverted to Ojora way to connect Boundary bus stop.

From Baale street to the Boundary roundabout is an appreciable movement.

The stretch of Mobil road both inward and outward at the moment is a fast moving one.

From High Bridge /Ijora Oloopa ramp to Total up is a fast moving traffic on both lanes 

However, shortly after Total by RRS junction we have flat beds trucks occupying one lane while the second lane is good to go For vehicular movement.

The movement of vehicles out of Apapa front Point road  through the Marine bridge to Iganmu is equally a fast moving traffic.
Officers are on ground doing the needful.
#FollowLASTMA

data.raw_text: Traffic violations contribute just a fraction to the problem. The basic problem is there’s just too many vehicles on the road, especially the 2-wheeled & manually-pedalled ones. Edsa & other major roads may be super highways but they may not be the super, shortest or best routes at all times. Arterial roads must be utilized to the fullest if we really want to decongest. Barangay & City roads must first be cleared of illegal structures, plant boxes, rolling stores, parked cars, OA clean & green projects, etc. And, oh, let’s not forget, also remove those obstructions called road & directional signs particularly those with political messages. Those signs make pedestrians walk on the streets & avoid RROWs contributing to needless traffic chaos. If we don’t reduce the number of vehicles owned by people, no amount of infra projects will ever catch up. It’s either the chicken or the omelet. Solution: Amend the archaic PH Transportation Code. It’s more than 50 years old. @HouseofRepsPH @senatePH @SayChiz @SpeakerMartinPH @bongbongmarcos
